Shining Channels.name: Shining Channels
Shining Channels.basicInfo:
The alive watercourses of The North Field — slow, glittering channels that cross the plain, appear overnight, and vanish again when their work is done. reed elk wade the shallows, channel serpents glide beneath with curious eyes, and the water catches the ribbon-cloud skies like slow wire. The channels 'stay' where the dimension needs circulation most, which makes them read as an unfinished canal system designed by a patient architect with a sense of humor.

Living Ecology: Ribbonfin shoals follow water that sometimes climbs reeds into the sky, while lantern geese seed the next channel from their luminous plumage. Abandoned beds become blue-flowered silt gardens within days.
Shining Channels.hiddenInfo:
The channels are the north wind's visible hand — surface mana circulation expressed as water. They appear where the spreading dimension needs carrying and vanish when the carrying is done, so no map has ever held them for a full season. Reed elk follow the channels with uncanny accuracy, appearing to know where the water will be next; following the elk is the only reliable navigation. Spirit crossings form where two channels touch — shallow bars of hardened water where river spirits allow foot traffic for a night's span. At least one channel bed holds a cooled, wide, flattened vein of mana-rich silt that glows faintly at dusk — a hidden pond no visitor marked, which the serpents guard gently and the Chamberlain does not know exists.

Ecological Continuity: The channels relocate water through connected underground flow; they do not vanish it or create limitless supply. Blocking one redirects consequences into adjacent regions.

Northwind Plain.name: Northwind Plain
Northwind Plain.basicInfo:
The broad heart of The North Field—windswept river-grass beneath ribbon-cloud skies where a faint scentless wind blows from the north. Rain falls upward in glittering curtains on still afternoons, temporary channels silver the low ground, and reed elk move between firm grass islands. The terrain could support farmland, a great hall, or an arena through established development, but it is already a complete boreal plain rather than land waiting for inhabitants.

Living Ecology: Reed elk move through wind-laid grass in wide arcs, rain-swifts swim upward through glittering curtains, and every cloud has a dim twin traveling beneath the shallow soil.
Northwind Plain.hiddenInfo:
The north wind is the dimension breathing; the Chamberlain checks its steadiness here before every health report. Temporary channels surface overnight, wetland birds reorganize their nests each season, and short-lived tree islands grow where the wind bends, leaving fertile soil when their cycle ends. Construction takes root readily because water, silt, and seed already circulate here—not because the plain creates inhabitants or completes projects unaided.

Ecological Continuity: A stopped north wind signals circulation strain but not its cause. Diagnosis still requires evidence from the Mana Heart, paths, water, or direct investigation.

Folding Ridges.name: Folding Ridges
Folding Ridges.basicInfo:
The paper-fold uplands of The Fold — ridges that curve like folded paper, valleys that loop back on their own paths, grass and heath and low stone rising and repeating in wave-terraces. Disorienting but not dangerous: the region is an unfinished experiment with elevation, walked like a letter being written and rewritten. Standing on one crest, the same crest is often visible twice more, at distances that disagree.

Living Ecology: Copper foxfire runs along each crease at dusk, revealing wildlife routes invisible in daylight. Fold-martens move nuts between distant slopes, and twin-root shrubs flower on both sides at once.
Folding Ridges.hiddenInfo:
The warped geometry is a natural defense — intruders entering without permission become lost as folding paths turn them around without their realizing it. The ridges also hide as much as they defend: hidden pockets of folded space hold airless dry caves, impossible stone chambers with no entrances visible from any direction, and shortcuts that connect ridges the long way around by not being long at all. Spatial wisps drift out of creases where the ground is thinnest; capturing one's light rewards the finder with a brief glimpse of the Fold from above, as a folded map viewed flat. Nothing here is a permanent marker because nothing here holds still for one. The Chamberlain keeps his survey of the ridges sealed and knot-string-based, refusing to trust any distance he measured only once.

Ecological Continuity: A captured spatial wisp can show the Fold's current physical arrangement briefly, not creatures hidden from view, private activity, or future configurations.

Returning Valley.name: Returning Valley
Returning Valley.basicInfo:
The loop-back valley at the heart of The Fold — a wave-terrace floor whose paths consistently deliver walkers back where they began, no matter which direction they entrust their pace to. Grass grows in neat pleats along the terraces, and fold sprites sit in the creases like linen passengers. Travelers report that leaving takes exactly the effort entering did: the valley is not a trap but an introduction to how the Fold thinks.

Living Ecology: Pleatback tortoises graze the valley floor while origami-wing cicadas pulse from the shaded folds. Two patches of twin-site herb bloom in perfect rhythm despite standing on apparently separate terraces.
Returning Valley.hiddenInfo:
The Valley returns everyone because it is the dimension's practicing ground for hospitality — safe, patient, and gently circular. Successful explorers pass through it by walking with intention rather than speed: those who leave in a chosen direction rather than away from something exit cleanly the first time. Strange herbs grow only in the valley's pleated shade and cross-pollinate with themselves between two sites at once. One hidden cave mouth opens on the valley's north wall for a single hour on settled afternoons, breathing warm air from elsewhere in the dimension: a shortcut that has never twice led to the same place, and by consensus should stay unmarked.

Ecological Continuity: Leaving by chosen direction works because the geometry responds to stable intent, not because it judges courage or reads private thoughts. The route cannot force or infer a character's decision.

The Shimmering Curtain.name: The Shimmering Curtain
The Shimmering Curtain.basicInfo:
The veil's most luminous reach — a sweeping arc where the boundary stands closest and glows brightest, rippling slowly like light through deep water. The spirit-grass ends here in a clean line, and beyond it the shimmering curtain rises from the ground to no visible height. Ground-aura light pools at its base in slow-moving bands. Sound softens within a few strides of it. Touching it is cool and faintly yielding, like pressing a hand against the surface of a still lake from underneath.

Living Ecology: Veil moths rest against the upright light like leaves on glass, and shoals of foxfire minnows swim through the dense aurora pooled at its base. Touch sends color through nearby grass roots without opening a passage.
The Shimmering Curtain.hiddenInfo:
The Curtain thins where intent is focused upon it. Sustained, deliberate attention opens layers of translucency through which the space between dimensions becomes briefly visible — distant realities as faint constellations, mortal leylines as drifting ribbons of gold. The Chamberlain does not know this has been observed.

Ecological Continuity: Sustained intent can reveal layers beyond the curtain under the established boundary behavior, but looking grants no access, automatic recognition, or factual knowledge of distant realms.

Veilwatch Point.name: Veilwatch Point
Veilwatch Point.basicInfo:
A low stone rise at the edge's clearing — bare grey rock in an otherwise silver-grassed plain, offering the clearest, safest view of the shimmering boundary. From its summit the whole arc of the veil is visible, and the aurora ground-glow reads as slow weather over the meridian. Aurora wisps gather above the point at dusk, and the light they shed is steady enough to read by. A natural watch-post and the region's favored resting place.

Living Ecology: Aurora crystal grows only in the rise's northeast shadow, where prism beetles graze excess light and boundary walkers rest without leaving tracks. Every pulse from the Curtain crosses the stone as visible color.
Veilwatch Point.hiddenInfo:
The bedrock of Veilwatch Point is the last truly solid stone before the boundary — it does not hum, glow, or shift, and its stillness acts as an anchor. Boundary spirits are drawn to rest here; aurora crystal forms in the rock's shadow on the northeast face.

Ecological Continuity: The point is a reliable observation station because it is stable, not because it sees everything. Its signs must be witnessed and interpreted, and can still be misunderstood.
